name: Ascent at Salt Flats
award: 2025 Federal 4% housing tax credit with noncompetitive state credit
headline: A 144-home, all income-restricted family rental community on city-owned land in Grand Junction, developed by Brikwell; CHFA lists it as a 2025 Federal 4% award.
why_it_matters: It shows a 4% deal made to work in a mid-size Western Slope city: free city land on a 99-year lease, bonds plus state credit, and a Prop 123 gap loan.

status.label: Credits awarded; closing and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA marks the credit amounts subject to change, and no public record found yet shows the financing closing or construction starting on the Ascent. The city's anticipated completion moved to Q3 2028.

next_step: Watch for the City Council item approving final land agreements, which the city says follows the tax credit award.

key_numbers.meaning: Studios to four-bedrooms for households at 30% to 70% of area median income, averaging about 58 to 59%.
About $21.1 million over the 10-year credit period; CHFA also issued $700,000 in noncompetitive state credit.
Issued by CHFA; the city handed CHFA $12,750,115 of its own bond cap for the project.

key_numbers.value: $2.52 million of city land for $100 a year
key_numbers.meaning: A 99-year ground lease; the land would give the city an 11% equity stake, which the parties expect to make the project tax-exempt.

background.text: The city bought the 21.78-acre Salt Flats parcel for $3.2 million, closing 9 January 2025: a $2.2 million Prop 123 land banking grant plus a $1 million city match.
Because state land banking money bought the site, 70% of the homes across Salt Flats must meet an affordability standard.

Ordinance 5275 (adopted 20 August 2025) leases 4.42 acres to Brikwell for 99 years at $100 a year; Brikwell may end the lease if it lacks a tax credit award, site plan approval or construction funding within five years, and the buildings revert to the city at the end.

Non-binding letters of intent (Resolutions 51-25 and 52-25) would convey the land as the city's in-kind equity once Brikwell wins tax credits, the land is subdivided and Council approves final agreements.

Brikwell funds all development costs and guarantees debt, completion and compliance; the city gives no guarantees and receives quarterly reports. The developer fee follows CHFA's QAP: 12% of total cost less land, developer fee and reserves.
Infrastructure for the site: a $2 million DOLA More Housing Now grant, an $800,000 city match and a $1 million seller contribution.

The city's preliminary plan marks Lots 400 (6.050 acres) and 500 (1.403 acres) for Brikwell apartments; a note says the site is mostly in FEMA flood zone X, with the southwest corner in zones X and AE.
